title: Spinach and Artichoke Dip Pizza
changes_from_base: The flavours of a warm spinach and artichoke dip, cream cheese, soured cream, garlic, herbs and parmesan, are spread over two par-baked bases and covered with mozzarella in place of the tomato sauce.
summary: Two pizzas that taste just like the famous spinach and artichoke dip, with a creamy herbed filling and melted mozzarella bubbling on top.
equipment: pizza stone or heavy baking tray
electric hand mixer or wooden spoon

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
tinned artichoke hearts, drained and roughly chopped
cooked spinach, chopped and squeezed dry (thawed if frozen)

steps.title: Make Dough
steps.text: Mix and knead water (340 ml), oil (27 ml), salt (2 tsp), flour (480 g) and yeast (2 tsp) into a smooth, pliable dough, cover and rise 30 min.

steps.title: Heat Oven
steps.text: Put the pizza stone on a lower shelf and heat the oven to 230 °C.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Halve the dough, pat each half into a 30 cm round, set on baking paper and rest 20 min.

steps.title: Make Topping
steps.text: Beat the cream cheese (225 g) slowly until smooth, mix in soured cream (115 g), oregano (2 tsp), basil (1 tsp) and chopped garlic (2 cloves), then fold in artichokes (330 g tinned, drained and chopped), spinach (225 g cooked, squeezed dry) and parmesan (30 g grated).

steps.title: Bake Bases
steps.text: Slide one base on its paper onto the stone and bake 5 min (keep the other covered), repeat.

steps.title: Top and Finish
steps.text: Spread half the topping over each base, scatter mozzarella (225 g grated), bake each about 15 min more until golden and bubbling, serve hot.

tips: Make sure cooked spinach is completely squeezed dry so it doesn't release water and make the pizza soggy or watery
Beat the cream cheese thoroughly until smooth before mixing in other ingredients to ensure an even, creamy texture throughout
These pizzas are best served hot straight from the oven when the cheese is still bubbling and the filling is warm
storage: Cool completely, then keep chilled for up to 2 days and reheat gently in a low oven until warmed through. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
